correctness.rationale: The exact single-symbol essential norm is m^{-alpha} because the associated weight equals (1-|z|)^alpha and (1-r^m)/(1-r) tends to m. Subadditivity gives the upper bound. For the lower bound, a finite set of distinct boundary points eta_j is chosen; explicit analytic peaks have weighted norm at most 2^{epsilon_n}, attain weighted value tending to one at their own radial targets, vanish locally, and are asymptotically disjoint. Their sum is weakly null in H^0_v and has norm tending to one. Compact operators therefore vanish on the test sequence, while the weighted evaluation of T yields the claimed sum. All parameter and boundary limits are stated; no numerical experiment is used as proof.

value.rationale: Exact additivity of the essential norm is not automatic for sums of operators: only subadditivity follows from the quotient norm in general. The result gives a closed formula for an entire natural family of finite sums and a reusable criterion for when distinct monomial boundary images prevent essential cancellation. It extends the known one-operator boundary calculation to a simultaneous finite family, with a sharp formula rather than an estimate. The result is limited to a clearly motivated standard weight and finite N; it does not claim a general composition-operator theorem.
